name: zrndr_draw_line16_clipped
description: zRndr_DrawLine16_Clipped clips a 16-bit line against an integer rectangle and rasterizes the surviving segment into a pitched framebuffer.
known_limits: VC5SP3 byte verification remains blocked: python tools/recoil.py verify vc5 0x499500 reports 649 unmasked mismatches with 40 relocation bytes masked, 13 trim nops, Binary Ninja body 717 bytes, and VC symbol 736 bytes. The reviewed diff shows broad control-flow/register-allocation and x87 clipping-source-shape drift rather than relocations or trailing padding.
functional_evidence: Binary Ninja assembly for 0x499500 validates Cohen-Sutherland outcode construction for both endpoints, trivial rejection when endpoints share an outside plane, x87 slope calculation for clipping, _ftol conversion when moving clipped endpoints to rectangle bounds, and final 16-bit Bresenham rasterization into dstPixels using gRndr_PitchBytes >> 1.

Binary Ninja keeps a limited reconstruction marker because x87 slope values and compiler-reused argument stack slots still render as decompiler artifacts; the assembly-level behavior and _ftol provider boundary are verified.
The native smoke verifies horizontal clipping, diagonal clipping, vertical clipping, and a trivial reject case against a {left=2, top=2, right=5, bottom=5} rectangle on an 8-pixel 16-bit pitch.
